title: A Strange Year
content: Imagine you have a magic window. Sometimes, when you look outside, the sun is shining very brightly and it feels very hot. Other times, you need to wear a warm jacket because it's cold. And sometimes, water falls from the sky!

title: Why does the weather change?
content: Why do you think we can't wear our cozy sweaters every day? What would happen if we wore a thick jacket on a very hot day?

content.title: The Changing Weather
content.description: Watch how the tree changes! It has green leaves in the heat, loses them when it's cold, and gets wet in the rain.

title: What are Seasons?
content: When the weather stays the same for a few months, we call it a Season! There are three main seasons we feel: Summer, Winter, and Monsoon (Rainy Season).

definition: A time of the year when the weather stays the same for a few months.
The hottest time of the year when we wear cotton clothes and drink cold water.
The coldest time of the year when we wear woolen clothes to stay warm.
The rainy season when we use umbrellas and raincoats.

question: What do we use in the Monsoon season?

title: Think About It!
content: Which is your favorite season? Can you explain to your friend why you like it the most? What is your favorite thing to eat during that season?

title: Connecting the Dots
content: Did you know that the clothes we wear, the food we eat, and even the festivals we celebrate change with the seasons? Farmers also wait for the Monsoon so their crops can grow!

title: My Season Drawing
content: Draw a picture of your favorite season. If it is Summer, draw a bright sun and an ice cream. If it is Winter, draw a snowman or a warm fire. If it is Monsoon, draw rain and a colorful umbrella!
Ask students what clothes they are wearing today and which season it is right now. Connecting it to their immediate environment helps solidify the concept.
Students often confuse 'Weather' and 'Season'. Weather can change every day, but a Season lasts for a few months.
